name: British Cape Colony
alt: Colony of the Cape of Good Hope

predecessors.name: Republic of Graaff-Reinet
predecessors.text: the Graaff-Reinet district and the eastern frontier of the Cape

successors.name: South Africa
successors.text: the Cape Province of the Union of South Africa

ledger.x: 1795: Britain takes the Cape from the Dutch.
August 1796: the British take the Republic of Graaff-Reinet.
1 March 1803: Britain returns the Cape to the Batavian Republic.
January 1806: the British retake the Cape.
1811: the Xhosa hold the Zuurveld.
1812: the Xhosa are driven back beyond the Fish River.
1820: the Albany district is established on the land between the Fish and the Keiskamma.
10 May 1835: Governor d'Urban annexes the Queen Adelaide Province.
December 1836: the Queen Adelaide Province is given up.
17 December 1847: Governor Smith annexes British Kaffraria.
17 December 1847: the Orange River becomes the northern boundary.
3 February 1848: Smith proclaims the Orange River Sovereignty.
23 February 1854: Britain gives up the Orange River Sovereignty.
7 March 1860: British Kaffraria becomes a separate Crown colony.
17 April 1866: British Kaffraria joins the Cape.
27 October 1871: Britain proclaims Griqualand West at the Kimberley diamond fields.
3 November 1871: Basutoland joins the Cape.
1877: Griqualand East is annexed.
12 April 1877: Britain annexes the Transvaal.
1878: Walvis Bay joins the Cape.
18 October 1880: Griqualand West is formally united with the Cape.
3 August 1881: the Transvaal is handed back.
3 August 1881: the Transvaal under British suzerainty.
1884: the London Convention replaces the Pretoria Convention.
2 February 1884: Basutoland becomes a separate colony.
End of 1886: Xesibeland is annexed.
1894: Pondoland is annexed to the Cape.
1895: British Bechuanaland joins the Cape.
31 May 1910: the Cape Colony joins the Union of South Africa.

wars.name: British invasion of the Cape (Battle of Muizenberg)
wars.outcome: The Cape passed to Britain; 'The VOC lost the colony to Great Britain following the 1795 Battle of Muizenberg'.

wars.name: Third Frontier War
wars.outcome: 'in February 1803 a peace was arranged, leaving the Xhosas still in the big Zuurveld.'

wars.name: Battle of Blaauwberg
wars.outcome: British victory; the Cape re-occupied on 8 January 1806 and ceded formally in 1814.

wars.name: Fourth Frontier War
wars.outcome: Colonel Graham's force drove the Xhosa back beyond the Fish River.

wars.name: Fifth Frontier War (War of Nxele)
wars.outcome: 'The British colonial authorities pushed the Xhosa further east beyond the Fish River to the Keiskamma River'; the Ceded Territories and the Albany district (1820).

wars.name: Sixth Frontier War
wars.outcome: Queen Adelaide Province annexed May 1835, disannexed December 1836; hostilities ended 17 September 1836.

wars.name: Seventh Frontier War (War of the Axe)
Eighth Frontier War (Mlanjeni War)
wars.outcome: Sandile and the other chiefs surrendered in February 1853; 'complete subjugation of the Ciskei Xhosa'; no boundary change on the page.

wars.name: Ninth Frontier War
wars.outcome: Gcalekaland 'was now administered as a British territory'.

wars.name: First Boer War
wars.outcome: Boer victory at Majuba (27 February 1881); Pretoria Convention of 3 August 1881 restored self-government under British suzerainty.

certainty.note: The northern frontier (the Bushmansland mountains) and the Xhosa frontier are approximate; the Great Fish River (1780) and Keiskamma (1820) are river lines.
The Orange River (1847), the Keiskamma-Kei rivers and the colonial proclamations are sharp lines; the Namaqualand and Kalahari edge and the Transkei, annexed in stages 1877-1894, are soft.
